newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Jan 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Jan 22.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.

- A luncheon between President Kim Young-sam and opposition party leaders on Tuesday ended without any change of stance by either sides. However Kim mentioned that "any law can be discussed in congress", seemingly backing up on the conservative party's former position of no revisions.
- A senior Russian deputy foreign minister, Grigory Karasin arrived in Pyongyang on Tuesday to discuss drawing up a new treaty to replace the one between the former Soviet Union and North Korea.
- Seoul temperatures are expected to fall yet further to minus 14 degrees Celsius (6.8 Farenheit) for an all time low this winter.

- The Trade Union Advisory Committee (TUAC) to the Organisation of Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) concluded Tuesday that South Korea's new labour law does not live up to international standards and urged the OECD to denounce South Korea's government.

- The National Congress for New Politics expressed deep concern on Monday that all posts in national intelligence and investigative agencies covering the next elections have recently been filled by those originating from Pusan and Kyungnam regions.

- China has officially warned Taiwan on its actions of sending nuclear waste to North Korea. A Chinese foreign ministry spokesman said on Tuesday:"Since Taiwan's decision to send nuclear waste to North Korea is a very sensitive issue, China will be watching the matter very closely."

- The won is falling and stocks are plummeting. The won price faced an all time low in nearly ten years on Wednesday at 852 won against the dollar. Meanwhile the stock index fell 27.92 points under the 700 line.
